blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 63 in June to 36 in October (−42.9%), and it took 15.0% of the city’s 247 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 11 in June to 10 in October (−9.1%), and it took 3.5% of the city’s 230 sales over the period.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Southwest Maple Ridge
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Confirmed form: freehold single-detached housing, with suites and garden suites as accessory uses in RS-1, and higher-density mixed-use forms enabled by the adopted Hammond Area Plan update near the plan area's commercial nodes.

Lot character — RS-1 zone minimums, as stated: the standard house zone is RS-1 (Single Detached Residential) under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%; accessory uses include Secondary Suite Residential and Detached Garden Suite Residential. These are zone minimums for RS-1, not a claim that every Hammond lot is that size.

Housing pattern the lots carry: Hammond's stock includes older single-detached houses around a historic commercial area, and the wider sub-area is mainly single-family development east of Hammond, under RS-1.

Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Highway) is a 55+ manufactured home park, ownership recorded as "Leasehold not prepaid-NonStrata" — the buyer owns the home and rents the pad; it is not a bare-land lot, not strata and not fee-simple land. The Maples Housing Co-operative (21570 Cherrington Ave, 31 semi-detached homes) is a co-operative, not a lot sale.
No ALR percentage split is stated or invented.

Serviced vs unserviced: in the Fraser River Escarpment policy area, City policy says septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers, and all drainage from new construction must connect to the City storm drainage system — the serviced position for new building in that policy area, as the City states it.

Market context, labelled correctly: SnapStats has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only; Maple Ridge is a SnapStats-covered community) — no detached figure is presented as a land figure.

blocks.text: Development proposals

items.t: Hammond Area Plan update: the Hammond Area Plan (OCP s. 10.5) has been given final reading and adopted by Council, and its OCP amending bylaw update enables mixed-use, higher-density buildings in the plan area and incorporates the additional density required by provincial legislation. This is plan enablement, not a lot offering.
Lougheed Transit Corridor: see — adopted Jan 27, 2026; the City states the plan does not immediately change any property's zoning, so it creates no lot inventory by itself.

Hammond recreation proposals: the City put two Hammond projects to an assent vote — the Hammond Aquatics and Recreation Centre at 11509 207 Street / 20601 Westfield Avenue (Loan Authorization Bylaw No. 8123-2026) and the Hammond Multi-Use Community Park at 20818 Golf Lane, the current Maple Ridge Golf Course site (Bylaw No. 8124-2026). Neither is a land sale.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: The official planning frame is the Hammond Area Plan (OCP s. 10.5), covering Hammond in the southwest corner; the City's neighbourhoods page also lists Port Hammond and Port Haney in this part of the city.

The Hammond Area Plan describes its area: "The Hammond neighbourhood is located in the southwest corner of Maple Ridge. It is bounded on the west by the City of Pitt Meadows and the Katzie First Nation, and on the south by the Fraser River; to the north are Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road commercial areas, and to the east is mainly single-family development."
Nearby areas: Pitt Meadows to the west across the municipal boundary, West Central and the Town Centre to the east, Port Haney at the sub-area's east edge, and the Fraser River along the south.

Main roads and transit: Lougheed Highway along the north side; Maple Meadows Station (20010 Dunn Ave) on the west side and Port Haney Station (22300 River Road) at the east edge, West Coast Express weekdays between Waterfront (downtown Vancouver) and Mission City; buses 743 and 744 loop through Hammond streets (207 Street, Lorne Avenue, Hammond), 701 runs along Dewdney Trunk Road, 791 along the north side, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs on the Lougheed Highway corridor north of the area.

Parks: Hammond Park, 20577 Lorne Avenue, has benches, a playground, a sport court, a tennis court and a pickleball court; Hammond Community Park is the site of the Larry Walker and Hammond Stadium ballfields, Hammond Hall and the Hammond Outdoor Pool; the Maple Ridge Golf Course is at 20818 Golf Lane in Hammond.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: OCP — contested citation, flagged, never resolved: The Hammond Area Plan is OCP s. 10.5, adopted, with a Hammond Development Permit Area (heritage) applying to properties within the Hammond Area Plan.

Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted Jan 27, 2026: the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted January 27, 2026 — Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 was given third reading and adopted at the January 27, 2026 Council meeting, following the January 20, 2026 public hearing; the corridor runs from the City's western boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, with growth directed around future Bus Rapid Transit stations at 203 Street, 207 Street, Laity Street and 216 Street. The City states the plan does not immediately change any property's zoning.

Escarpment rules: the Fraser River Escarpment policy area (City Policies 6.23 and 6.24) is bounded by 207 Street to the west, 124 Avenue to the north, 224 Street to the east and the escarpment crest along the south; all drainage from new construction must connect to the City storm drainage system, properties within 300 m of the crest require a geotechnical report attached to a Section 219 covenant before a building permit, and properties within 100 m of the crest require a detailed geotechnical report addressing potential seismic slope failure; in the policy area septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers.

ALR rules — general framework, no ALR ground documented in this sub-area: where a parcel is in the ALR, subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Hammond began as Port Hammond Junction. The City records that the Hammond brothers, William and John, donated land to the CPR on the condition the first railway station in Maple Ridge be built in Hammond, and the junction served as a supply depot as the community grew around the station, yards and a cedar mill — the origin of the heritage stock and the Hammond Development Permit Area.
The Hammond Aquatics and Recreation Centre (Bylaw No. 8123-2026) and Hammond Multi-Use Community Park on the golf course site (Bylaw No. 8124-2026) were put to residents.

No recreation centre or library branch sits in the southwest. The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place in the Town Centre to the east, and Maple Ridge Public Library is at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road — land here is bought for the Hammond / river / station position, with a drive for those facilities.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Southwest Maple Ridge

This is built-out urban ground — older single-detached houses around Hammond's historic commercial area and mainly single-family development to the east, under the RS-1 zone. A buyer searching "acreage" who lands on this sub-area is buying a large urban house lot, not an acreage — and the diligence that matters is the escarpment, floodplain and SSMUH frame in, not farm diligence.
The ground in Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Excluded forms: Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Highway) is a 55+ manufactured home park recorded as "Leasehold not prepaid-NonStrata" — the buyer owns the home and rents the pad; it is not a bare-land lot, not strata and not fee-simple land. The Maples Housing Co-operative (21570 Cherrington Ave) is described by CHF BC as 31 semi-detached homes held as a co-operative — the buyer holds co-op membership/shares, not a strata lot and not fee-simple land.

The land-value lever here is density, not acreage: Eligible single-detached and duplex lots may carry up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. That — not subdivision into acreages — is what a "land" buyer is actually pricing on this area.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC. The official planning frame is the Hammond Area Plan (OCP s. 10.5), covering the Hammond neighbourhood in the southwest corner of the city; the City's neighbourhoods page also lists Port Hammond and Port Haney in this part of the city.

The Hammond Area Plan describes its area this way: "The Hammond neighbourhood is located in the southwest corner of Maple Ridge. It is bounded on the west by the City of Pitt Meadows and the Katzie First Nation, and on the south by the Fraser River; to the north are Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road commercial areas, and to the east is mainly single-family development."
Search and alternate names: "Southwest Maple Ridge" (board name), plus the City names buyers also use — Hammond, Port Hammond and Port Haney.

Main roads and transit: Lougheed Highway runs along the north side; Maple Meadows Station (20010 Dunn Ave) serves the west side and Port Haney Station (22300 River Road) sits at the east edge, with West Coast Express trains running weekdays between Waterfront (downtown Vancouver) and Mission City; buses 743 and 744 loop through Hammond streets (207 Street, Lorne Avenue, Hammond), the 701 runs along Dewdney Trunk Road at the north edge, the 791 runs along the north side to Braid Station, and the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs on the Lougheed corridor north of the area.

Landmarks are urban and historic, not rural: Hammond Park at 20577 Lorne Avenue (benches, playground, sport court, tennis and pickleball courts); Hammond Community Park with the Larry Walker and Hammond Stadium ballfields, Hammond Hall and the Hammond Outdoor Pool; the Maple Ridge Golf Course at 20818 Golf Lane; Hammond's historic commercial area is a named feature of the neighbourhood in the Hammond Area Plan; larger shopping is Haney Place Mall, 11900 Haney Place, to the east; the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place in the Town Centre.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Fraser River Escarpment: the Fraser River Escarpment policy area (City Policies 6.23 and 6.24) is bounded by 207 Street to the west, 124 Avenue to the north, 224 Street to the east and the escarpment crest along the south. All drainage from new construction must connect to the City storm drainage system; properties within 300 m of the crest require a geotechnical report attached to a Section 219 covenant before a building permit; properties within 100 m of the crest require a detailed geotechnical report addressing potential seismic slope failure; in the policy area septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers. A big lot near the crest does not build like a big lot elsewhere — this is the single most important land diligence item in the sub-area.

Floodplain: Hammond fronts the Fraser River to the south; the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), a covenant on title identifies construction in the floodplain, no habitable floor space may be located below the flood construction level on affected lots, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties — do not underwrite suite income on a floodplain lot.

If a strata purchase is made elsewhere in Maple Ridge (redirect case): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. None of it applies to a fee-simple Southwest Maple Ridge lot purchase itself. Note the limit: Val Maria's 55+ restriction is a manufactured-home park tenancy rule, not a strata bylaw, and is not governed by these sections.

blocks.text: Good to know about Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Hammond began as a railway bargain: The City records that the Hammond brothers, William and John, donated land to the CPR on the condition the first railway station in Maple Ridge be built in Hammond; the junction (Port Hammond Junction) served as a supply depot as the community grew around the station, yards and a cedar mill — which is why the oldest, largest lots in the sub-area cluster around the historic core and the two West Coast Express stations bookend it today.

The OCP number itself is contested: 10.5 position and adopted status are the settled facts. Any older page or feature sheet quoting an OCP number for this area should be verified against the City's current bylaw list before it is relied on.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Southwest Maple Ridge
Known stock inside Southwest Maple Ridge: ONE pad-rental park (Val Maria) and ONE housing co-operative (The Maples — built homes, not a manufactured-home park).
The parks and communities

items.t: Val Maria: Plainly: a home here sits on a rented pad — the buyer owns the home (a chattel) and rents the pad; the buyer does not own the land, and there is no strata, no Form B, no depreciation report and no CRF. The tenancy is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act. Listings record the sub-type as Mobile Home / Manufactured Home and the ownership as "Leasehold not prepaid-NonStrata," and listing pages for the park are classified Southwest Maple Ridge.
The Maples Housing Co-operative: CHF BC describes it as 31 semi-detached homes located between Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway, a 2-minute drive from Ridge Meadows Hospital.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: The official planning frame for the area is the Hammond Area Plan (OCP s. 10.5), covering the Hammond neighbourhood in the southwest corner of the city; the City's neighbourhoods page also lists Port Hammond and Port Haney in this part of the city.

Where the mobile-home stock in this sub-area sits: Lougheed Highway runs along the sub-area's north side and carries its one manufactured home park (Val Maria at 21163); The Maples co-op is at 21570 Cherrington Ave, between Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway.

Transit — West Coast Express: Maple Meadows Station (20010 Dunn Ave) serves the west side of the sub-area and Port Haney Station (22300 River Road) sits at the east edge; trains run weekdays between Waterfront (downtown Vancouver) and Mission City. Buses: the 743 and 744 run between Meadowtown and Haney Place via Maple Meadows Station and loop through Hammond streets (207 Street, Lorne Avenue, Hammond); the 701 runs along Dewdney Trunk Road at the area's north edge; the 791 runs along the north side to Braid Station; the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs on the Lougheed Highway corridor north of the area.

Commute: the Golden Ears Bridge at the area's west side connects Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows to Langley and Surrey, and the City states Golden Ears Way will be expanded from two lanes to four between the Highway 7 interchange and 210 Street, with detailed design underway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect park-home buyers in Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Escarpment / floodplain: The Fraser River Escarpment policy area (City Policies 6.23 and 6.24) is bounded by 207 Street to the west, 124 Avenue to the north, 224 Street to the east and the escarpment crest along the south; properties within 300 m of the crest require a geotechnical report attached to a Section 219 covenant before a building permit, and properties within 100 m of the crest require a detailed geotechnical report addressing potential seismic slope failure; in the policy area septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers. Hammond fronts the Fraser River to the south; the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), no habitable floor space may be located below the flood construction level on affected lots, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties.

blocks.text: Good to know about Southwest Maple Ridge

items.t: Septic is a live issue in the escarpment policy area: City policy says septic fields shall be avoided and all new residences shall require sanitary sewers — confirm sewer connection status on any older Hammond home, and check whether a specific lot sits within 300 m (or 100 m) of the escarpment crest before pricing a rebuild.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: streets and boundaries

items.t: The Hammond plan divides the area into four precincts: North Hammond, Upper Hammond, Lower Hammond and the Maple Meadows Business Park.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: the housing stock

items.t: Hammond's stock includes early-1900s single-family houses, a historic commercial area, a 5.4-hectare baseball park and a 16-hectare golf course, per the area plan.
Lower Hammond, fronting the Fraser, is described in the plan as having a rural character not typically found in single-detached suburban areas.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The updated Hammond plan focuses growth near Maple Meadows Station and introduces Maple Meadows Residential and Maple Meadows Mixed-Use designations with increased density near transit.
Near the station, the plan allows 8–12 storey mixed-use buildings, while protecting employment lands in the Maple Meadows Business Park precinct.
A Hammond Heritage Character Area and a Hammond Development Permit Area apply inside the plan area; Upper Hammond carries the heritage precinct policies.
Ground-Oriented Residential lots here can support single-detached, duplex, triplex and fourplex forms, with up to six units within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Part of the q̓ic̓əy̓ Slough sits at the western edge of the Business Park precinct and provides natural drainage for the area.
Hammond Elementary at 11520 203 Street doubles as a local voting place, and the plan names it inside the heritage-side precincts.
The golf course lands at 20818 Golf Lane were the proposed Multi-Use Community Park site — that proposal ended with the October 2026 vote.
Golden Ears Way, at this area's west side, is the road TransLink is widening from two lanes to four between the Highway 7 interchange and 210 Street.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: development and new projects

items.t: Guide-specific item: both Hammond Recreation Ready projects were defeated at the October 17, 2026 assent vote and will not proceed as proposed; City staff were to seek direction from the new Council.
Guide-specific item: the Hammond Area Plan update was adopted November 25, 2025.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: costs and taxes

items.t: The 2026 flat water fee is $859.25; Maple Ridge is also a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so residential owners must declare.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: getting around

items.t: Maple Meadows and Port Haney are consecutive West Coast Express stations; the full run is 69 kilometres and about 75 minutes end to end, per TransLink.
The 791 bus links Haney Place to Braid Station via Maple Meadows Station, Hammond Road and Harris Road, per the TransLink timetable.

blocks.text: Southwest Maple Ridge: risks and due diligence

items.t: Floodplain is the first check in Lower Hammond and the Business Park: Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 8121-2026 designates floodplain, sets flood construction levels and setbacks, and regulates fill placement.
No habitable area may be built with its floor system below the Flood Construction Level on a designated lot under that bylaw.
Heritage rules are the second check in Upper Hammond: confirm whether the lot sits in the Hammond Heritage Character Area figure in the plan before planning exterior changes.

faq.a: No named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering is known.
faq.q: Is there bare land for sale in Hammond / Southwest Maple Ridge?

faq.a: RS-1 minimums are 668.0 m² lot area, 18.0 m width and 27.0 m depth, with maximum lot coverage 40% under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 s. 605. Those are zone minimums, not a subdivision promise for a specific parcel.
faq.q: How big does a lot have to be to subdivide or build?

faq.a: One secondary suite per lot inside the house (maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the floodplain), and eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws.
faq.q: Can I put a suite or extra units on a lot here?

faq.a: No — Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties, and no habitable floor space may sit below the 6.7 m flood construction level on affected lots.
faq.q: Can I have a rental suite on a floodplain lot?

faq.a: Lots within 300 m of the crest need a geotechnical report on a Section 219 covenant before a building permit; within 100 m, a detailed report on seismic slope failure; drainage must go to the City storm system, septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers in the policy area.
faq.q: What does the escarpment mean for building?

faq.a: No — not as a market. The sub-area is built-out urban ground under RS-1 zoning (668.0 m² minimum lots). What trades is large urban house lots. Buyers who need true acreage need a different sub-area; buyers who want a big Hammond lot with suite and SSMUH potential are shopping the right ground for that different product.
faq.q: Is there any real acreage for sale in Southwest Maple Ridge?

faq.a: Only down to the RS-1 floor — 668.0 m² lot area, 18.0 m width, 27.0 m depth — through the City's subdivision process under the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 4800-1993 (City source), and lots in the escarpment or floodplain frames carry the added reports and covenants in. There is no route from an RS-1 lot to "acreage lots."
faq.q: Can I subdivide a big Hammond lot into smaller lots?

faq.a: The policy area (207 Street west, 124 Avenue north, 224 Street east, the crest along the south; City Policies 6.23 and 6.24) requires drainage to the City storm system; within 300 m of the crest, a geotechnical report on a Section 219 covenant before a building permit; within 100 m, a detailed report on seismic slope failure. Septic fields are to be avoided and new residences require sanitary sewers. Price the reports and the covenant into the lot, not after.
faq.q: What do the escarpment rules do to a lot near the Fraser River crest?

faq.a: No. Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties, secondary suites are not permitted within the floodplain area, and no habitable floor space may sit below the 6.7 m geodetic flood construction level on affected lots.
faq.q: Can a floodplain lot carry a rental suite?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — listings record the ownership as "Leasehold not prepaid-NonStrata," the park owns/controls the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Plainly, a home on a rented pad is not land ownership. There is no strata and no Form B.
faq.q: In Val Maria, do I own the land?

faq.a: The provincial Regulation frames a 55+ park as one where sites are reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (or two or more tenants, at least one of whom has reached 55), and the landlord may refuse an assignment where the proposed purchaser does not meet the age requirement — so a couple where one partner is 55+ fits the provincial model. The strata spouse/caregiver exemptions do not apply to a park. Val Maria's own written rule governs day to day: get it in writing.
faq.q: Is Val Maria really 55+ — and does my younger spouse fit?

faq.a: Confirm in the current written park rules before writing an offer around a pet.
faq.q: Can I have a dog at Val Maria?

faq.a: No. The Maples (21570 Cherrington Ave) is a housing co-operative of 31 built semi-detached homes.
faq.q: Is The Maples a manufactured-home park I can buy a pad in?

faq.a: No — on October 17, 2026 voters rejected both Hammond borrowing bylaws: the Aquatics and Recreation Centre at 11509 207 Street / 20601 Westfield Avenue (6,841 yes, 14,218 no) and the Multi-Use Community Park at 20818 Golf Lane (6,209 yes, 14,797 no). The City states the projects will not proceed as proposed.
faq.q: Did the Hammond recreation projects get approved?

faq.a: Partly — portions of Lower Hammond are in the Fraser River floodplain, and all of the Maple Meadows Business Park precinct is in the floodplain, per the area plan. The plan carries a Hammond Area Floodplain figure, and the City's 2026 floodplain bylaw sets construction levels for designated lots, so check the specific address.

Two — Maple Meadows Station at the west side and Port Haney Station at the east edge both sit on the West Coast Express line between Mission City and Waterfront. Trains run Monday to Friday, westbound in the morning and eastbound in the afternoon, with no weekend or statutory-holiday service.
faq.q: Which train stations serve this side of Maple Ridge?

faq.a: Council adopted the Hammond update on November 25, 2025 as part of the city-wide area-plan package. It directs growth around Maple Meadows Station, adds the Maple Meadows Residential and Mixed-Use designations, and increases density near transit as provincial legislation requires, while protecting employment lands.
faq.q: What changed in the Hammond plan in 2025?
